title: Firstborn from the Dead
summary: Jesus entered the gates of darkness not in defeat but to plunder, and led out the captives in victory. His rescue mission continues.
exhortation: Our focus this morning: "He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, that in everything he might be preeminent."

When Jesus rose from the dead, every enemy cowered in defeat. Psalm 68 says, "God shall arise, his enemies shall be scattered; and those who hate him shall flee before him! As smoke is driven away, so you shall drive them away; as wax melts before fire, so the wicked shall perish before God!"

When Jesus died, he entered the gates of darkness not in defeat but to plunder. He went into the depths on a holy rescue mission, breaching the walls and smashing the gates. He devastated the stronghold of darkness and left it shocked and defenseless. The captives held in chains for so long, he set free, and his enemies were helpless to resist. When he rose from the dead, he led out the captives in victory. As Psalm 68 also says, "You ascended on high, leading a host of captives in your train."

And Jesus isn't done with his rescue mission. There are still captives to be found and freed, walls to be breached and gates to be torn down. Aren't you thankful the rescue mission continues? It's the reason we're here. We were captives in chains in deep darkness, and Jesus set us free. Now he gives us a purpose and a mission as part of his gospel army. It's time for us to breach some walls and smash some gates, because the light has shone in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.
prayer: Jesus, thank you for descending into the darkness, storming the gates and breaching the walls where we were held captive, and rescuing us from utter darkness. What a wonderful Savior you are.

I pray for those who are fearful of the day ahead, looking at a mountain of things to do and difficulties to face. As they fix their eyes on you, Jesus, wash away their fear and anxiety, and give them your supernatural joy and the peace that surpasses understanding. Remind us who you are and what you've done, and that it can never be undone. We didn't do it in our own power. If we had, it could be undone. You did it once for all. It was finished by you on the cross. When you rose in victory, you led a host of captives in your train, and that's us. You lifted us up with you, the firstborn from the dead. Remind us who you are, Lord. In Jesus' name, amen.
